articleTitle: Full-Duplex V-Band Radio over Fiber Transmission Based on Microwave Photonic Self-Heterodyne Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: The millimeter-wave frequency band possesses abundant available spectrum resources and has become a critical pillar for 5G/B5G wireless networks. Meanwhile, the V-band (50GHz-75GHz) has become a research hotspot for the next-generation wireless communication technology due to its characteristics of both spectrum license-free and large bandwidth. This paper proposes a full-duplex V -band radio over fiber transmission system based on microwave photonics self-heterodyne conversion, aiming at the high-capacity and low-cost demands of dense millimeter-wave wireless access networks. The system utilizes the suppression of double-sideband optical signals with the same carrier to achieve optical heterodyne beat frequency generation for downlink millimeter-wave communication, as well as uplink millimeter-wave signal carrying and self-heterodyne downconversion processing, which can significantly reduce the implementation cost of remote radio units and central stations. The research on the microwave photonics signal processing-based millimeter-wave communication system and network architecture has certain guiding significance and provides a new solution for achieving low-cost, long-distance transmission and ultra-high-capacity ultra-dense millimeter-wave access networks.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Evaluation Model for Global Port Production based on AIS Big Data
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Ports are important hubs for international logistics, and port operation status directly reflect the smoothness of the global logistics supply chain. The dynamic evaluation method of port production are investigated. Firstly, the big data of global ship Automatic Identification System (AIS) is used to analyze the spatiotemporal trajectories of ship berthing and unberthing. Secondly, key indicators of port production such as the numbers of berthing and anchoring ships, the time of ships in ports and the anchorages are quantitatively calculated, and then a production dynamic evaluation model of global ports is proposed base on AIS big data. Finally, taking the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach as examples, the impacts of the COVID-19 on port production state and berthing service level are quantitatively analyzed.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Area Detection Method based on Ray Crossing
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: In flight test, the airplane is constrained by various complex operational limits, which define its flight envelope. Traditionally, ground monitoring personnel need to constantly pay attention to whether the test aircraft is maneuvering within the restricted range to ensure flight safety, but this can easily cause fatigue for monitoring personnel and lead to misjudgment. To address this issue, we first study the algorithm for the relationship between points and enclosed areas, and then design an area detection method based on ray crossing. Next, the closed area detection module is implemented by C # programming to realize the rapid detection of targets in closed space such as envelopes. Additionally, in order to improve the reusability and generalization, we encapsulate the detection module code as a dynamic link library file. Several flight data were had been used to verify this method. The results using flight data have demonstrated that this method is precise and effective. Detection results can provide alarm sources for the monitoring alarm software, further support the monitoring personnel to make timely decisions.

articleTitle: Fragment: A Horror Game Prototype Utilizing a Dynamic Difficulty System through Agent Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Balancing the difficulty aspect in video games to address the skillsets of varying players has always been a challenge for video game developers. This is potentially a huge waste of development time, a portion of which could be allotted to developing more important aspects of a game instead, such as its atmosphere and story. The horror game genre is heavily reliant on building up its story and atmosphere, which take up a lot of development time to get both elements to an acceptable level. The development of Fragment, a horror game prototype, seeks to address this by implementing a Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA) System through its gameplay mechanics. With the help of Dynamic Difficulty, developers may not need to allot a lot of time to difficulty balancing. The researchers were able to determine that the game was able to address varying player skillsets using the DDA System, and successfully create a game with a horror atmosphere.

articleTitle: Backpropagation Neural Network – Based Prediction of Crack Depth in Fly-Ash Geopolymer Concrete with Akaike and Bayesian Information Criterion
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Concrete have been a major contributor in the environmental pollution particularly its the carbon footprint during its production. In connection with the sustainable development goals (SDGs), the use of alternative materials with lower emissions and footprint could alleviate and help in the expanding problem of global warming. This study evaluated the potential of fly-ash (FA) geopolymer concrete (GC) and create a machine learning based model using backpropagation neural network (BP-NN) for predicting crack depth. The results of the modelling exhibited that the governing configuration of the crack forecast model is 2-5-1 (input-hidden-output) (I-H-O) with Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 9.71%. Additional layer of evaluation was implemented in the identification of the governing model which includes the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC). Lowest AIC and BIC values were observed in the governing model structure which suggested that it is the best among the features evaluated. Moreover, the variable contribution (VC) to the crack depth model development were assessed using Garson's algorithm (GA) and the results showed that the pulse wave travel time is the parameter with the highest contribution to the crack depth model development.

articleTitle: Dynamic Digital Twin Modeling towards Ship Operation and Maintenance Process
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Ships consist of a lot of large and complex equipment, and equipment failures can lead to serious accidents. Nowadays, a few ships have online operation monitoring, and the most widely used ship maintenance method is not able to solve the problem in time when there is an unexpected failure of ship equipment. Therefore, this paper proposes a dynamic modeling approach of digital twins toward the ship operation and maintenance (O&M) process to solve the unexpected problems of ships. Firstly, a ship O&M ontology model is built by summarizing key equipment operating parameters of the ship and the ship maintenance methods. Then, the operating parameters are modified dynamically in the O&M ontology by using the Jena API based on the real-time state parameters of the ship in the twin data model. Afterward, the operating status of the equipment and maintenance are reasoned by O&M SWRL rules and fed to the physical entity in time. Finally, in order to verify the feasibility of the approach, the digital twin O&M model of a ship is constructed by ontology modeling in the O&M process of a ship. The experimental results show that the approach can dynamically monitor the operation process of the ship and analyze the maintenance method in time when the main engine of the ship fails.

articleTitle: Optimizing Privacy and Convenience in the Sharing Economy: A Blockchain and Multi-Agent Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Given the concerns over data privacy violations in the sharing economy, this paper introduces a framework that combines blockchain with Multi-Agent technology. The framework aims to decentralize data storage, thereby reducing the risks associated with centralized systems. This initiative is particularly timely, considering the vulnerabilities of centralized control systems to cyber-attacks that could lead to widespread data leakage. Within this setting, blockchain ensures data privacy and security for users while permitting only transaction participants to understand the encrypted data. The integration of Multi-Agent technology significantly enhances transaction efficiency. It provides a more robust mechanism for supply-demand alignment and participant matching, which are critical aspects in the sharing economy. A proof-of-concept prototype has been developed to substantiate the decentralized nature of the framework. It shows promising potential to mitigate prevalent issues of data abuse and exposure, thereby paving the way for a more secure and efficient sharing economy.

articleTitle: SDCM: An Efficient Camellia Oleifera Fruits Detection Algorithm in Dense Occlusion Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: To realize intelligent management in the Camellia oleifera fruit industry and foster the efficient growth of its supply chain, the accurate identification and detection of Camellia oleifera fruits are essential. However, in natural environments, these fruits exhibit challenges such as clustering, mutual occlusion, and obstruction by leaves. This paper proposes a Camellia oleifera fruits detection algorithm based on an improved YOLOv7 deep convolutional neural network, which is referred to as the SDCM network model, and add the function of counting the number of fruits. We introduce an enhancement to the backbone layer of the YOLOv7 model by incorporating a module called SDCM (Shortcut and Dilation Convolution based Module). This module enriches multiscale edge information, enabling the network to extract features more effectively, thus improving detection accuracy. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy of the SDCM network model is significantly improved compared with the original YOLOv7 model, and the detection performance of the model in this paper is superior compared with other classical detection models. By enhancing the detection accuracy of the model and adding the function of fruit counting, the model in this paper can provide more reliable and accurate detection performance and the function of predicting fruit yield for the development of the Camellia oleifera fruit industry, improve the production efficiency, and reduce the artificial resources.

articleTitle: Icon-based Coding Software with Multi-user Evaluation Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: As the Software (SW) cantered society has emerged, SW-based problem-solving capabilities emphasized in all areas of society. It is a trend that universities are obliged to do SW basic education for non-major students and they are carrying out programming education. This study derives grammatical elements based on conciseness, generality, and efficiency among the design principles of programming theories and based on it, compares and analyses visual programming language and diagramming language. In this paper, we introduce a new coding education software ICAN for all ages. It supports icon coding and debugging mode, students can check wrong part or value with callstack while programming. In addition, ICAN provides multi-user tournament-style evaluation mode.

articleTitle: Exploring the Depths of Bluetooth Attacks: A Critical Analysis of Bluetooth Exploitation and Awareness of Users
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Bluetooth technology has become ubiquitous in modern devices, facilitating wireless communication and connectivity. However, Bluetooth is susceptible to various security vulnerabilities that can be exploited through attacks like Bluesnarfing, Bluesmacking, and car whispering. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of different Bluetooth attacks, examining their mechanisms, procedures, impacts, and limitations. The researchers demonstrate Bluesmacking, Bluesnarfing, and car whispering attacks, elucidating how attackers can deny service, steal data, and secretly record conversations. Comparative analysis categorizes the attacks based on vulnerabilities, severity, and technical limitations. Additionally, a survey of 35 Filipino participants aged 19–58 measured awareness regarding Bluetooth security. Results showed low knowledge of attacks among respondents, despite frequent Bluetooth usage. While most expressed general concern about Bluetooth security, greater awareness is needed to mitigate risks. This paper concludes that continuous research and education on evolving Bluetooth threats is essential to strengthen security and protect users' privacy.

articleTitle: Advancing Earthquake Prediction: A Comprehensive Review of Data Science Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: This paper delves into the transformative potential of data science for earthquake prediction techniques. Through a thorough literature review, it explores methodologies spanning machine learning, deep learning, time series analysis, signal processing, Bayesian models, and data integration, assessing their relevance in earthquake forecasting. Key algorithms, including Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting Machine, General Linear Model, and Artificial Neural Networks, are used to interpret seismic data. Using simulation results, this study underscores the promise of these varied methods in earthquake prediction. The research concludes by pinpointing prospective areas of study and emphasizing the need for cross-disciplinary cooperation to surmount challenges in earthquake prediction, ultimately aiming to reduce the catastrophic effects of earthquakes on societies and infrastructure.

articleTitle: Empirical Assessment of the MAFIS Mobile App's Usability Based on the People at the Center of Mobile Application Development (PACMAD) Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: The primary objective of this research was to evaluate the usability aspects of the MAFIS mobile app among Philippine National Police (PNP) personnel. The study assessed effectiveness, efficiency, learnability, memorability, error handling, and cognitive load. The research employed a surveybased methodology aligned with the PACMAD usability model. The findings indicated that the app consistently demonstrated high efficiency, surpassing expectations regarding task completion time, page duration, and interaction requirements. The evaluated effectiveness categories performed highly satisfactorily, signifying the app's successful achievement of its intended goals. Learnability was deemed high, as users perceived the app as easy to learn and quickly acquired the necessary skills. Moreover, the app exhibited a relatively high level of memorability, enabling users to reuse it without external assistance. The study also highlighted the app's strong error handling and recovery performance, providing effective support and informative error messages. Users experienced a manageable cognitive load, enabling them to complete tasks within allocated time frames. Overall, the research concluded that the current usability of the MAFIS mobile app was acceptable while recognizing the subjective nature of usability influenced by individual user factors. This research contributes to the existing literature on evaluating the usability of mobile applications in Philippine government institutions, offering valuable insights for developers and designers. Future studies could expand the sample to include other government agencies and explore novel methodologies for assessing usability.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Based Model Reconfiguration Method for Ship Design Using NSGA-II
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Ship design is a crucial step in ship-building process, and the design method is relatively homogeneous. However, the traditional ship design approaches have long design periods, consuming much manpower and physical resources. Besides, traditional methods take much more time and it could be further upgraded to meet specific demands. With the increasing diversity of ship demands, the ship design model is being paid much attention in recent years. In this paper, a digital twin-based reconfigurable ship design method is proposed. This digital twin- based model contains physical entity, virtual model, interconnection model, digital twin data, as well as service support services. A digital twin-based model of ship is established. Based on such digital twin model, the NSGA-II is utilized to generate an optimal reconfigurable ship design scheme, considering various performance demands. Case study is conducted to validate the reconfigurable ship design method based on digital twin model. The results shows that the NSGA-II method can generate a reconfigurable design solution for different performance demands.

articleTitle: Towards Unsupervised Analysis of Dakar Motorcycle Rally Data
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: The Dakar Rally is an annual motorcycle rally event consisting of 10 or more stages. Such rallies are popular sports that require team and rider strategy to perform well. We explored the data from the 2022 and 2023 Dakar Bike Rally to determine the most important factors to be considered in building a good race strategy. We consider the effect of teams, sponsorship, experience, the different stages and their conditions on the final rankings. To do so, we use unsupervised clustering on the times series from the different rally stages. Autoencoders and statistical testing was used to determine the most important factors that determined final standings in the race. Our findings show that the initial stages were key in determining the final outcome of the rally. Moreover, teams, nationality and experience of the riders do not significantly contribute to the final race standings. In addition, sponsorship also seemed to have an effect on the finishing standing of the participants. Furthermore, stages that start after a rest day were more critical in winning the race.

articleTitle: Neglected Cyber Threats on the Rise: Combatting IoT Botnet Infection Techniques through the Elucidation of Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices have become prevalent in this age. The overwhelming amount of neglected IoT devices has become a powerful platform for enforcing botnets and launching DDoS attacks. Several IoT botnets have been developed and are constantly evolving due to increased security measures placed by information security professionals - some of which are: Bashlite, Mirai, and Torii. Machine learning is emerging as an effective tool for botnet detection - distinguishing malicious traffic in the network from normal traffic. Although numerous studies have already been conducted about botnet detection using machine learning algorithms, more is needed to explore machine learning models explicitly catering to each type of IoT device and the variation of botnets. Hence, this study will serve as an empirical basis for using machine learning algorithms to identify and counteract IoT botnets, underscoring the vital role that proactive security measures play in protecting interconnected networks and neglected devices. Four IT experts with different extensive job experiences and expertise were interviewed to collect valuable insights and data on the topic.

articleTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis & Data Mining on NBA Match Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Basketball has been a popular domain for researchers to collect and analyse vast amount of data. With the data of players, teams, games, and seasons, researchers can gain useful insights into players and matches. Nowadays, machine learning is an important tool for data analysis and prediction and has achieved powerful effect and inspiring accuracy in existing research of NBA data. In this paper, we are motivated to research on the factors that are essential for NBA match outcome prediction and how to build the most effective data set and most powerful models to make the best prediction. Multi- variate regression analysis was used to analyse the importance of factors and how these factors influence the outcome of a match. Then machine learning models, like naive bayes, random forest, Logistic regression, K nearest neighbors and LDA are applied. Finally, an experiment was conducted in search of the best data setting. It turns out that the most significant factor is the recent win rate, while the best model in accuracy is logistic model with average accuracy of 67% over all seasons and the best strategy is generating data from last season.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Government Response Analysis to COVID-19 in Delta Variant Stage based on FCM-DID Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Aimed to provide insight into the global trend of COVID-19 during the Delta variant stage and offer recommendations for effective epidemic prevention policies. In this study, we propose a novel data-driven causal inference model combining fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering and difference-in-difference (DID) for multiple time series data. Based on the FCM clustering, a set of panel data with parallel trends can be obtained for further DID analysis. By comparing the change in the outcome variable between the treatment and control groups within each cluster, before and after the intervention, the causal effect of each cluster on the outcome variable is estimated. In government response analysis to COVID-19, the daily updated data of 196 countries all over the world during the transition phase from the outbreak of the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant to the discovery of Omicron was collected. Application of our method shows that adopting restrictions on internal movement policies had a substantial impact on preventing the spread of the pandemic. The FCM-DID approach we proposed is useful for identifying and comparing the effects of policies on the outcome of different groups, thus can well evaluate the effectiveness of implemented policies and provide valuable guidance for decision-making in future public health crises.

articleTitle: DARPA Electronics Resurgence Initiative 2.0 Program Layout in Fiscal Year 2024
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Electronics Resurgence Initiative (ERI) 2.0 has been issued by Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency in the Fiscal Year 2024 budget estimates. ERI 2.0 consists of 32 programs with total cost of $710 million, indicating the development trend forward next generation microelectronics. First, the background, key funding parts (materials & integration, architectures and designs) and typical research findings of ERI are analyzed to present its overview and importance. Second, the overall program layout characteristics of ERI 2.0 are analyzed from different layout changes like being started or terminated. Third, all the programs are analyzed from five research areas including next generation microelectronics, advanced electronic components, microsystem integration technology, advanced computing architecture and facility, and security of electronic equipment and network. For every area, the budget funding is counted and contrasted with the past to show the research change. To further analyze program layout, the mission accomplishment, forward plan and application of all the programs from different technical areas are studied, to overview current advances and look ahead to the next generation microelectronics. The research of ERI 2.0 in this article will be great importance for following research, evaluation, layout and industrial development of future microelectronics.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Decisions: Exploring the Impact of Data Mining in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: In the healthcare sector, data mining stands as a crucial tool for analyzing vast patient datasets to unearth significant revelations. This manuscript provides a comprehensive exploration of data mining's contributions to healthcare, spanning from pandemic research, treatment efficacy assessment, predictive modeling, insurance fraud detection, medical device optimization, to streamlined hospital management. It delves into various data mining techniques such as clustering, classification, statistical analysis, unsupervised pattern recognition, and web-based data scrutiny, emphasizing their relevance in healthcare contexts. Algorithms like the Naïve Bayes Classifier and K-means clustering are underscored for their prevalent use in health-related scenarios. The treatise wraps up by shedding light on the emerging trajectories for healthcare data mining and pinpointing exciting avenues for impending inquiries.

articleTitle: Research on Internet Governance Behavior Based on Internet Social Responsibility
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: As the major groups of the Internet, Internet users have an important impact on Internet governance activities. It is of great significance to understand the characteristics of Internet users' behavior of Internet activities to improve the level of Internet governance. Based on the multi-agent modeling method, the Internet governance model including the government, Internet media and Internet users is constructed. The model is simulated by using the Python platform. From the perspective of Internet users' social responsibility, the comparative study on the social responsibility of Internet users. The results show that social responsibility of Internet users has a normative effect on Internet users' participation in Internet governance, and government information disclosure, credibility, the degree of legal perfection and the Internet media attention to the event, the clarity of Internet users have an alternative role in social responsibility. The model is modeled by case study in this paper. In the last, this paper puts forward relevant countermeasures and suggestions.

publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Computing and Big Data (ICCBD)
abstract: Computing and big data are emerging research fields that have recently drawn much attention from computer science and information technology as well as from social sciences and other disciplines. ICCBD 2023 is organized by University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, China and supported by Southern University of Science and Technology, China, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China. And the goal is to provide an international forum for exchanging ideas and information on current studies, challenges, research results, system developments, and practical experiences in these emerging fields.
